title: CNI state drift and IP lease leak - scratchpad
content:
Summary:
We saw a progressive degradation in pod scheduling across multiple clusters in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 starting ~2024-11-07T03:40Z. Symptoms looked like CNI failing to allocate IPs (pods stuck Pending with `failed to find available IP address`), intermittent pod networking failures (NetworkUnavailable), and a correlated increase in node-level pod eviction events due to node pressure perceptions (kubelet reporting CNI errors). Early indicators pointed to an IPAM leak/state drift inside the CNI plugin, resulting in address exhaustion for certain node subnets.

Impact:
- ~5% of clusters had elevated Pending pods for 20-90 minutes.
- Small fraction (<0.7%) of customer-facing inference pods were restarted or delayed — transient 95th p99 latency blips observed in infra metrics.
- No data loss, but degraded availability for ephemeral workloads and job retries.

Detection timeline (rough):
- 2024-11-07 03:38Z: Pager alert: `k8s_pod_pending_count` alarm triggered for cluster-prod-usw2 (threshold 50).
- 03:40Z: Oncall pulled `kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase=Pending` -> many pods with `FailedCreatePodSandBox` / `failed to find available IP address` in events.
- 03:48Z: `kubectl describe node <node-1>` showed CNI error events and warning: `NetworkPlugin cni failed to set up pod "..." network: failed to allocate ip`
- 03:55Z: Pulled CNI daemonset logs (calico-node/amazon-vpc-cni) - saw repeated errors: `ipam: allocation failed: no available addresses` and `failed to release address: route not found` in some contexts.
- 04:02Z: `calicoctl ipam show` (staging query replicated to prod read-only) showed a leak: number of allocated addresses exceeded expected active pods count by ~12% on a subset of nodes.
- 04:15Z: `journalctl -u kubelet` on affected node showed frequent `CNI DEL failed` / `CNI ADD failed` interleaving with kubelet restarts (kubelet OOM kill happened earlier in a different incident for that node).

Hypothesis (root causes under consideration):
1) Race between kubelet and CNI during pod deletion: kubelet restarts or SIGKILL leads to incomplete CNI DEL calls, leaving IPAM entries orphaned.
2) CNI plugin returns success to kubelet but failed to cleanup routes; on retries the plugin double-allocates or fails to re-use leaked/ghost leases.
3) Underlying host networking (iproute/netlink) transient failures prevented DEL from removing host-side state, leaving partial allocations visible to calicoctl but not reconciled.
4) A recent change in the CNI (github PR referenced below) introduced an edge-case where DEL errors are swallowed and not retried.

Commands & checks executed during triage (copied for runbook):
- kubectl get nodes -o wide --show-labels
- kubectl describe node <node-x> | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector=status.phase=Pending -o wide
- kubectl logs -n kube-system calico-node-<id> --tail=200
- calicoctl ipam show --show-allocations (read-only view copied to investigator sandbox)
- journalctl -u kubelet -n 500 --no-pager
- ip -4 addr show dev <eni-device>  # verify host addresses and leaked routes
- ss -tunap | grep kube-proxy
- curl -sS http://localhost:9094/metrics | grep cni

Immediate mitigations applied (fast roll):
- 04:35Z: cordoned ~8 nodes with highest ip utilization and scheduled pods were drained (kubectl cordon/evict) to slow appetite for new IPs.
- 04:42Z: restarted calico-node daemonset on 6 affected nodes (kubectl rollout restart ds/calico-node -n kube-system) — immediate partial recovery on 4 nodes where leases reclaimed.
- 04:55Z: increased alerting to include `cni_ip_lease_utilization > 80%` (temporary) and created a high-frequency sampling for the next 2 hours.
- 05:10Z: rebooted one node after kubelet OOM evidence; post-reboot, ip allocations normalized for that host.

What helped vs what didn't:
- Restarting calico-node often reclaimed addresses when the underlying host netns was intact.
- Rebooting kubelet/host was durable for nodes with suspected kernel/netlink state corruption.
- Simple `kubectl delete pod` of ghost pending pods did not always free up IPs; indicates leak persisted at IPAM level, not only k8s object state.

Short-term follow-ups (<=72h):
- Add a scheduled reconciler job that compares live pod IPs vs IPAM DB and attempts safe release of orphans (dry-run first). (Owner: Liam)
- Patch CNI to retry DEL on transient netlink errors and log a structured trace when DEL fails (Owner: Ava, PR linked).
- Add runbook steps for controlled node reboots vs calico-node restart (Owner: Priya).
- Create alerting: `cni_ip_lease_utilization > 70%` and a synthetic test that repeatedly creates/deletes pods to validate IP reuse.
- Run canary in staging cluster with high churn (simulated pod churn) to validate fix.

Longer-term corrective actions (backlog):
- Implement graceful kubelet shutdown extension (give CNI time to DEL) or coordinate CNI DEL retries across kubelet termination lifecycle.
- Improve CNI instrumentation (trace ids per ADD/DEL to correlate logs).
- Consider IP pool sizing changes or secondary pool fallback for high-churn node pools.
- Postmortem write-up and customer-facing RCA if needed.

Runbook draft excerpt (to be expanded):
- Trigger: Pending pod ratio > 2% for 10m AND events include `failed to find available IP address`.
- Initial checks: list Pending pods -> identify node selectors -> `calicoctl ipam show` for those nodes.
- Safe remediations order: cordon -> restart calico-node -> wait 2m -> if not recovered, evict noncritical pods -> if still not recovered, reboot node (escalation required).
- Do NOT immediately resize pool without SRE approval; resizing can mask leak without root-cause fix.

Open questions / unknowns:
- How often does kubelet crash/fast-restart correlate with these leaks historically? Need correlation query.
- Are there specific workloads or CRI runtimes (containerd vs cri-o) that surface this more often? (No signal yet.)
- Does our version of the CNI match the upstream fix in PR #1234 referenced in linked_artifacts?

Owner notes / notes to self:
- Avoid broad restarts during customer peak; prefer node-by-node approach.
- Keep the calicoctl operations read-only in prod. Any WRITE should be run from a controlled SRE bastion and documented.

Suggested Jira tasks (short):
- SRE-3214: Implement CNI DEL retry + structured logs (blocker for next patch).
- SRE-3220: IPAM orphan reconciler job (dry-run -> write) + canary plan.
- SRE-3221: Runbook: CNI leak playbook and runbook test (book a ~2h verification window on staging).

References & links used during triage:
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/oncall-incident-2024-11-07
- Candidate PR (fixes DEL swallow): https://github.com/calico/cni/pull/1234 (referenced for context)
- GitHub PR for our internal cherrypick: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/789

Next steps for this doc:
- Convert scratchpad to formal incident review after 72h when we have reconciler run outputs.
- Add concrete metric graphs (iputil, pending pods, kubelet restarts) embedded in postmortem.
- Assign owners for each follow-up and set due dates in the SRE sprint.

Rough notes (free-form):
- I think the leak has two flavors: 1) soft orphans (IP visible in ipam but routes removed) and 2) hard orphans (kernel/netlink state corrupted). Different remediations.
- We should avoid the temptation to expand IP pools as first-line; that just increases our blast radius.
- Need to test CNI DEL in accelerated failure modes (fast kill of kubelet, simultaneous node ENI detach).

-- Priya Nair (oncall)
